newsitem.title: UK: UK lottery directors to pay bonuses to charity.
newsitem.headline: UK lottery directors to pay bonuses to charity.

text.p: Directors of British national lottery operator Camelot Group Plc have agreed to make payments to charity from forthcoming bonus entitlements, Camelot said on Friday.

The plan ended a public row with National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith over hefty bonuses for Camelot directors. Smith, the minister responsible for arts and culture, said he now regarded the matter as closed.

"We will publish in July, for the widest consultation, our detailed proposals for putting one billion pounds ($1.6 billion) over five years into health and education projects and for seeking an efficient non-profit operator after 2001," he said

Camelot's licence expires in 2001. The new Labour government was "outraged" last week when bonus payments helped to inflate Camelot's executive wage bill 40 percent to 2.3 million pounds while money raised for good causes fell.

Smith said Camelot would pay to charity a sum equivalent to the bonuses recently paid to directors. The company's main executives will contribute to a charity fund from their forthcoming long-term bonus entitlement.

Interest from undistributed prize money over the next four years will go to the lottery good causes instead of to Camelot, a potential boost of 24 million pounds. Camelot is also to discuss with the government how a non-profit lottery operator might work.
